content:
#1 Hi all,

I have been running experiments for a while to try to see if you could get coding agents to generate useful things, like a model of a very odd programming language in Agda. I have results and they heavily involve category theory.

I am trying to create minimal logic constructions using preorders, lax operators, and a hard choice of refinement over equality. I have a number of further architectural constraints. The overwhelming majority of what comes out is *very* well known mathematics and aligns well with physics basically because I am pouring my physics intuition in here (was a junior prof in theoretical physics at some point in the past).

One of the main points of this experiment is not new math, but a working coding harness for coding agents that can be verified to work mathematically. A straightjacket if you will, and one that balances strictness with expressivity. Signs are very good so far.

I would really like some sparring with people who know category theory and who do not shoot me on sight for taking coding agents to bear on their favourite philosophy, logic, math and/or physics. In exchange I can show you what coding agents *may* be capable of, *when properly steered*. No AGI-golems here - I just use off-the-shelve coding agents.

If you are interested, just raise your hand or ping me

content:
#6 If this is what it seems, its a programming language largely determined by the constraints it models and instantiating the math it describes. So odd is the word - even the descriptions are odd.

I use coding agents all the time, but am hyperaware this is controversial in some circles. FWIW, I think of coding agents as context-indexed stochastic functors, where context is built out of training data, inference infra, codebase fundamentals and the user prompt. Hallucinations are context errors and therefore influencable. This coding harness idea is just an expression of this belief.

To my mind locally preordered categories are like a poor man's version of category theory - what is your interest?

content:
#10 I did an Agda exercise showing that the sum of abelian group homomorphisms is an abelian group homomorphisms today using GPT to help me with some of the proofs.

I think it will be easier to show that abelian group homomorphisms form an abelian group altogether than this one fact, which I had to divide into eleven steps to break down the use of various laws. (Of course, I didn’t use the TIO browser, that would be awful).

I decided I wanted at least one result like this one before I proceeded.

I like the topic here so I think I’ll come back to it with some more exercises I’ve done in not too long. I like the idea of partially ordered abelian groups as locally preordered.

I take it you might want some time to gather your thoughts but definitely say more about what you’re interested in and that you’ve tried out.
